LESSON: GUIDED WRITING

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: GERMAN
Strand: WRITING Theme 2. Family: Nuclear Family
Topic 3.9: Guided writing

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Guided writing. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: what they do during the week and share with peers. What do you enjoy writing?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify basic German orthography rules
2. write texts observing German orthography rules
3. appreciate the role orthography plays in writing
4. identify German sounds combination in writing
5. write creative texts for learning
6. appreciate the role of writing in everyday life
7. identify vocabulary in writing for learning
8. write texts using acquired vocabulary for communication

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: GUIDED WRITING
Subject: GERMAN · Grade: Grade 4
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Guided writing helps you succeed in GERMAN. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: GUIDED WRITING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify basic German orthography rules

What this means
In this part you learn to identify basic German orthography rules. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify basic German orthography rules.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Guided writing”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify basic German orthography rules. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Write texts observing German orthography rules

What this means
In this part you learn to write texts observing German orthography rules. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: write texts observing German orthography rules.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Guided writing to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can write texts observing German orthography rules. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate the role orthography plays in writing

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the role orthography plays in writing. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the role orthography plays in writing.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the role orthography plays in writing. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Identify German sounds combination in writing

What this means
In this part you learn to identify German sounds combination in writing. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify German sounds combination in writing.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Guided writing”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify German sounds combination in writing. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 5: Write creative texts for learning

What this means
In this part you learn to write creative texts for learning. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: write creative texts for learning.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Guided writing to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can write creative texts for learning. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 6: Appreciate the role of writing in everyday life

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the role of writing in everyday life. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the role of writing in everyday life.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the role of writing in everyday life. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Guided writing is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Guided writing”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify basic German orthography rules)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Guided writing to a partner. (skill: write texts observing German orthography rules)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: appreciate the role orthography plays in writing)

Example 4: Read a short paragraph about “Guided writing”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify German sounds combination in writing)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Guided writing to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify basic German orthography rules.
3. Practise this skill: write texts observing German orthography rules.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate the role orthography plays in writing.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Guided writing from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Guided writing: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 4 learner study Guided writing?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. what they do during the week and share with peers. What do you enjoy writing?
2. Why do you write?
3. Why is writing things down important?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Guided writing means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify basic German orthography rules.
5. Be able to: write texts observing German orthography rules.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
